newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian construction shares shed around three pct.
newsitem.headline: Belgian construction shares shed around three pct.

text.p: Shares in Belgian construction groups Franki NV and CFE SA fell around three percent in early trade on Wednesday, but dealers said the price movements hid different stories.
Franki's 18 franc, 3.41 percent, drop to a 510 franc all-time low was part of a longer-term downtrend that probably had not seen bottom, they said.
CFE's 270 franc, 2.84 percent, decline to 9,230 francs was just profit-taking after recent strong gains.
"I could see Franki going down to 450 francs. There's still room to underperform," BBL analyst Francois Poullet said.
Poullet rated CFE a 'hold'. "It's fairly valued at current levels," he said.

Franki has fallen almost continuously in the past 12 months from a high of 780 francs on February 6, 1996, in the wake of an agreed takeover of Belgian building materials group Desimpel by British conglomerate Hanson.
In contrast, CFE's share took off in recent months, adding nearly 30 percent since last November.
Analysts said that although both were active in civil engineering and construction, the difference centred on CFE's additional interests in dredging.
Analysts expected Franki, 60 percent owned by family owned Belgian Groep Van Roey, to report it barely broke even in 1996 after losing 138 million francs in 1995 and 458 million in 1994.
It is due to release 1996 figures on April 22.
Franki said last year it might join its foreign operations with local partners.

But while CFE's building activities were still only slowly recovering from two tough years, analysts did not expect CFE and Franki to seek to collaborate along the lines of the planned alliance between German rivals Holzmann and Hochtief .
CFE is 43 percent held by France's much larger Dumez-GTM SA, a unit of Lyonnaise des Eaux.
